speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: You try the front door. It does not open. It is not a door.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: It is a very well-painted rectangle on a wall. Somebody has painted a tiny brass knocker. You knock on it.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: It makes a sound like knocking on a wall.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: You try the door. It does not open. You peek through the window: it is a painting of a window, and beyond it a painting of a living room with a painting of a family.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: They are smiling. They have been smiling for six years.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: The door has no handle. The house has no inside. Behind the facade there is just room for a ladder and a young woman painting the same window for the thousandth time.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: She looks at you. She looks away. She has the face of someone who has meant to write home for years.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: You try the door. It is open! It is a closet.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: It contains a mop, a bucket and a sign that says: IF YOU ARE READING THIS, SMILE.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: The front door is still painted on. Someone has written under the knocker: 'Come round the back, we have a kettle.'

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: The painted window now has a real curtain, hung over it by a citizen who wanted one. The family in the painting has acquired a moustache.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: The door has a handle now, and the house has an inside: two chairs, a table, a tea tray. The paintbrush has been left on the ladder, for good.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
current_text: The closet is a closet. The sign says: IF YOU ARE READING THIS, YOU DO NOT HAVE TO SMILE.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
current_text: Attention, citizens! Today is a PERFECT day! The weather is APPROVED!

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
current_text: Please continue to be happy, as scheduled! This has been your Deputy Minister of Good News!

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
current_text: Attention, citizens! A reminder that smiling is MANDATORY! Those found frowning will be helped! Thank you for your cooperation!

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
current_text: Attention, citizens! (a pause) Attention, citizens! (a very long pause) ...the announcement has been completed. Please clap.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
current_text: Great news, citizens! New this season: Approved Hat Sizes! There is one! Please wear it!
new_text: Great news, citizens! This season brings one Approved Hat Size! Choice has never been easier!
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
current_text: Attention, citizens! {villain_title} reminds you that he loves you, and that he is watching. These are the same statement.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
current_text: Attention, citizens! Spontaneity Thursday is coming! Please prepare your spontaneity in advance! Please be surprised at three o'clock!
new_text: Great news, citizens! Spontaneity Thursday approaches! Please rehearse your surprise. We expect a natural performance at three!
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
current_text: Attention, citizens! Please remember: the exits are for ENTERING. The entrances are for EXITING.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
current_text: Anything else is an unapproved Direction.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
current_text: Attention, citizens! All is well. All has always been well.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
current_text: This message is brought to you by the number one.
new_text: A correction: this message has always been correct.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
current_text: Great news, citizens! The Wrinkles do not exist.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
current_text: Please report anyone who exists. This has been your Deputy Minister of Good News!

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
current_text: Attention, citizens. (a cough) This is a loudspeaker. Nobody is on the other end.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
current_text: Please do whatever you like. That is all.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
current_text: Attention, citizens. A reminder: you do not have to smile. (a pause) Also: you may smile. We are very easy.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
current_text: Attention, citizens. A pigeon is using the loudspeaker. Please stand by.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
current_text: Attention, citizens! Hats of any size are now permitted. Hats of negative size remain a mystery.
new_text: Attention, citizens! Any hat size is permitted. You may finally stop thinking about hat sizes.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
current_text: Attention, citizens. He was afraid, and we were afraid of him. Please be gentle with yourselves.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
current_text: Attention, citizens! Spontaneity Thursday is now all days. Please prepare to be surprised constantly.
new_text: Attention, citizens! Spontaneity is no longer limited to Thursday. You may disregard this reminder.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
current_text: Attention, citizens. The exits are open. The entrances are open.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
current_text: The walls are still walls. Please do not run into them.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
current_text: Attention, citizens. All is not well. It will be.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
current_text: It is a lot of work. Thank you for helping.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
current_text: Attention, citizens. The Wrinkles were real. Please thank them.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
current_text: They are in the cellar. There is tea.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Great Doors

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Solid gold, ten metres tall, polished until you can see your own worried face in them. They open before you touch them. That is the worst part.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The great doors swing open, silent and perfectly balanced. Beyond them, a long hall, a red carpet and a smell of floor wax and lemons. Somewhere, a very long way away, someone is humming.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: 'Welcome,' says a tiny, polite voice from nowhere. 'Please wipe your feet. Please wipe your opinions.'
new_text: 'Welcome,' says a quiet voice. 'Please wipe your feet. You are expected.'
writer_note: Castle tone: removes opinions punchline while preserving the unsettling welcome.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Great Hall

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A hall the length of a street, and not one speck of dust. Guards stand at attention every ten paces, each one exactly the same height. (A battle.)

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Portrait Gallery

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Thousands of portraits of one man, in order. Each is a little taller, a little straighter, a little more perfect than the last. A story event.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Curator's Rounds

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A curator with a feather duster and a very small smile patrols the side gallery. Anything crooked, he straightens. Anything alive, he dusts. (A battle.)
new_text: You see a curator patrol the side gallery, feather duster in hand. He straightens each frame without looking at its face. (A battle.)
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Forgotten Alcove

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A side door behind a very large frame: a small alcove where the old portraits went when they were replaced. A dead end with a prize, then back to the gallery.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The old portraits lean against the wall, face to the plaster. Behind the last one: a small bag someone left. 'In case anyone comes looking for the real one,' says a note. You take it and go back.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Mirror Knight

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A knight made entirely of mirror plates, each of them showing only one face. It moves exactly like you. Then it stops doing that. (A battle.)

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Hall of Mirrors

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A hall of mirrors that reflect only him. A deck challenge: how well do you lead with your own face?

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The One Honest Mirror

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A small, dusty mirror in a closet, hung by someone who had to hide it. It shows whoever is standing in front of it. A dead end with a story.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Quiet Room

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A room of mirrors where, for once, nobody is reflected at all: they have been turned to face the wall. Rest here. Restore HP.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: You sit on the floor between mirrors that show only plaster. It is, for a few minutes, the most peaceful room in the Capital. Somebody has left a mug of tea and a biscuit.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The biscuit is a little crooked. You eat it.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Desk of Correction

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A long brass desk, a stamp and a form: 'FORM OF CORRECTION'. A deck challenge: do you have the bodies to fill the form?

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Ministry Clerk

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A clerk at a tall desk, stamping everything that moves. Quite fast. Quite sad. (A battle.)
new_text: You face a clerk at a tall desk. His stamp falls rapidly; his eyes stay on the paper. (A battle.)
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: The Chief Corrector

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: The head of the Ministry of Correction: white gloves, kind eyes, a ruler. She is very, very gentle. That is what makes it frightening. (Elite)

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: The Chief Corrector sits down on her own chair, very carefully, and lays her ruler on the desk. 'I corrected eleven thousand,' she says.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
current_text: 'I never once asked what was wrong with them. Please. The door on the left. Go and look.'

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Corrected

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A long ward behind the Ministry where citizens who were 'corrected' are kept. A dead end with a story, then back to the corridor.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Hall of the Four Wings

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A circular hall with four doors, one for each Path. Each wing is a dead end: a place where he 'perfected' that Path. Visit any, all or none; then take the corridors on.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Four great doors, each in its own Path's colour: red with a dumbbell, gold with a ladle, violet with a notary's seal, green with a seed.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Over each, a brass plate: 'PERFECTED'.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Gourmand Wing: The Laboratory

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The doppelganger's laboratory: vats of Special Sauce, rows of masks, one very worried technician. (A battle, then lab notes.)

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Racks of masks line the walls, each one a face: the Grand Chef, smiling, smiling, smiling. On a clipboard by the door, in a neat hand:

speaker: (narration)
current_text: 'LAB NOTES: Subject A (the Grand Chef) proved resistant to persuasion. Resolved by substitution. The substitute is cooperative, and does not argue about the sauce.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: All Gourmands to be fed the sauce. They will be happier. They will be less themselves. This is a feature.'
new_text: 'All Gourmands to be fed the sauce. They will be happier. They will no longer need to choose for themselves.'
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: You tear the last page off the clipboard. Under the neat hand, in the margin, in a small shaking one: 'He did not look at the faces. He never looked at the faces.'

speaker: (narration)
current_text: You fold it into your pocket and go back.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Beefcake Wing: The War Room

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A war room full of maps, flags and one very large, very empty throne: the place where the coup was planned. (A battle, then the orders.)

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A table covered in maps of the Gainlands, with little red pins in every mill and wheel. On a clipboard:

speaker: (narration)
current_text: 'COUP ORDERS: Remove Grandmaster Flex. Remove his weights, his protein, his gymnasium. Observe.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: When the champion is sufficiently weak, he will no longer be a disagreement. NOTE: do not underestimate him. He does a lot of stretching.'
new_text: 'When the champion is weak, he will no longer be a disagreement. NOTE: he continues to train without the weights. Observe carefully.'
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: In the margin of the orders, in a smaller, shakier hand: 'He was not weak. We took everything from him and he got stronger. I do not understand it.'

speaker: (narration)
current_text: 'I have asked the champions to be weak. They will not.' You fold the orders and go back.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Necrocrat Wing: The Notary's Office

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A tall office of notarized, filed and countersigned paper: the authorization that took the Necrocrats. (A battle, then the paperwork.)

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Shelves of paper to the ceiling, every sheet stamped. On the top of the pile, a single form:

speaker: (narration)
current_text: 'FORM 1-A (NOTARIZED): Authority over all Necrocrat government is hereby transferred to His Perfection. Reviewed. Approved.
new_text: 'FORM 1-A (NOTARIZED): Authority over all Necrocrat government is hereby transferred to {villain_title}. Reviewed. Approved.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Filed. VALID. NOTE: the Necrocrats will obey this, because it is their nature to obey a valid form.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: I did not need to force anyone. I needed only to be correct.'

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Wraith's last words, as it folds: 'The authorization is valid.' Then, very quietly: 'It was never right.'

speaker: (narration)
current_text: You take the form. It can be revoked, you suspect, on a technicality. You go back.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Refusemancer Wing: The Greenhouse

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A glass greenhouse where something glowing and green grows in a single pot. The Rot began here. (A battle, then the seed.)

speaker: (narration)
current_text: In the middle of the greenhouse, under a glass dome, a single seed sprouts, glowing sickly green. A label on the pot:

speaker: (narration)
current_text: 'THE SEED: Nature is untidy. Nature is inefficient. Nature disagrees with itself.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A seed, properly corrupted, can be made to agree with me. Plant in the Archdruid. Observe.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: NOTE: it will spread. I cannot say I am sorry about that. I am very busy.'
new_text: NOTE: it will spread. What grows will be orderly. I believe she will thank me.'
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The dome is cracked. The glowing seed lies in the dirt and is, for a moment, just a seed. In the label's margin, in a smaller hand: 'She was grieving. I told myself that made it a kindness.'

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Somewhere in the Verdant Dump, if the Dump is free, a flower opens. You go back.
new_text: You leave the cracked dome behind and return to the hall.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Servants' Corridor

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A narrow back corridor where the castle's servants work, silent and very fast, in matching grey. They do not smile. They have stopped. (A battle.)

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Grand Staircase

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A staircase so grand it has its own staircase. Every step is exactly the same height. It is exhausting. A story event.
new_text: You face a vast staircase. Every step is the same height; you cannot see the landing from the bottom. A story event.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Wing Vault

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Where the two ways round the wings meet: a small vault of confiscated things. Treasure.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Archive Door

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A tall oak door with a brass sign: 'ARCHIVE OF GOOD INTENTIONS'. A warden stands in front, arms folded. (A battle.)

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The sign is older than the rest of the castle. It is painted by hand. Under it, in different ink, someone has written: 'He meant well.'

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Early Journals

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Shelves of journals in a young man's handwriting: the years before the throne. A story event.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Reading Room

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A quiet reading room, a lamp, a chair. Someone used to read here. Rest and restore HP.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: You sit in the old reading chair. It is worn exactly where one person sat, every night, for a long time. The lamp has a small, hand-made lampshade. Something about it is very, very human.
new_text: You sit in the reading chair. One person has worn a hollow in its seat. Beside you, lamplight shines through a handmade shade.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Blueprint Vault

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A side vault of blueprints: the sound reforms he drew up before it all went wrong. A dead end with a prize, then back to the reading room.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Plans for wells. Plans for a school lunch. Plans for a bridge that was actually built.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: They are beautiful. They are so good. You roll up the best and take it, with something in your throat.
new_text: You follow the lines of the plans with one finger. Then you roll up the best and take it. Your throat tightens.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Escalation Shelf

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A single long shelf where the reforms are filed in order. Each is a little bigger than the last. A deck challenge: can your deck keep its footing?

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Archive Automaton

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A tall brass automaton that files, stamps and shelves. It has been told the archive is complete. It is very sure. (Elite)

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Last Journal

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A single book on a stand, still open. The last page is still wet. A story event: the moment you see him as he sees himself.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A lectern in the middle of a round room, a book open on it, a pen beside the book. The ink on the last page is still wet. He wrote this today.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Model Warden

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The last guard before the Chamber of the Model: a warden whose job is to keep everyone away from the table. (Elite)

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Warden steps aside. Through the doors: a huge round room, a vaulted ceiling and, on a table the size of a house, a perfect miniature of the whole kingdom.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Somebody is bending over it, moving a tiny house one centimetre to the left.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Scale Model Chamber

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A giant model of the whole kingdom, and the man who rearranges it by hand. {villain_title}, {villain}. (Boss: three phases)

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Chamber of the Model is round and domed, and in its centre stands a table the size of a house: a perfect miniature of {kingdom}.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Roads, rivers, four districts, a hundred thousand tiny houses. Every one of them is exactly where he wants it.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A man in a pressed grey coat and a thin gold circlet stands with his back to you, moving a tiny cottage one centimetre to the left with a pair of tweezers.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The model lies in pieces. A hundred thousand tiny houses on the floor, all in the wrong places, and somehow they look better.
new_text: You stand among the pieces of the model. Tiny houses lie scattered across the floor. The table no longer holds a kingdom.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: {villain} sits among them, small, in his pressed grey coat, and does not move for a long time.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Hall of Mirrors

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Every mirror shows only him. They turn to look at you and, for a moment, one of them hesitates. Reveal cards until the first unit: if its attack is 3 or more, a mirror will let you through (and show you, briefly, yourself).

speaker: (narration)
current_text: If not, they will look through you and it will hurt.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Desk of Correction

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A FORM OF CORRECTION asks for a list of bodies: names, numbers and heights. Five cards are revealed; if at least two are units, you have enough people on your form to get past the desk. If not, the stamp comes down.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Escalation Shelf

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Every reform on the shelf is bigger than the last: school lunches, lunch rules, lunch inspectors, inspector rules. Five cards fall off; if at least two are infrastructure, your deck holds. If not, the shelf comes down on you.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Improved Portraits

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Thousands of portraits of one man, one a year. In the first he is a thin young clerk, anxious and kind, smiling at nothing in particular.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Each one is a little straighter, a little taller. By the last he is eleven feet tall, with no wrinkles and a smile that does not move. Under each: 'IMPROVED.'

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Study them closely, from the first to the last

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Look away and breathe

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Take a gold frame off the wall and sell it

speaker: (narration)
current_text: You look at them all, in order. The anxious clerk grows steadily less anxious, and steadily less there. You find the exact portrait where it happens: the tenth.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: In the ninth he looks so tired, and so sincere. You will not forget it. You see through the frame.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: You look at your feet. The carpet is red, and a little worn in the middle. That, at least, is honest. You feel a little steadier.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The frame comes off with a squeal. Somewhere an alarm goes off, very politely: 'Please do not remove the improvements.' A hand-sized portrait falls and cuts your hand. The frame is worth a lot.
